audit_question.question: After configuration-entry StoreLogs failure, does setState(Follower) synchronously invalidate the next leader-loop guard, preventing consumption of a commitment advance caused by F4's subsequent voter-map replacement?
audit_question.importance: If the replacement voter map advances the recorded commitment index and the leader consumes that advance, earlier outstanding entries could be applied or completed using support from the replacement configuration. The observed volatile advance alone does not establish that consequence.
contexts: StoreLogs returns an error, potentially after partial writes
Retained voter reports permit advancement under the replacement voter map
Pending commitment notifications during transition to follower
event_paths: dispatchLogs -> StoreLogs error -> respond(error) -> setState(Follower) -> return
appendConfigurationEntry continuation -> latest configuration replacement -> commitment.setConfiguration -> recalculate -> possible commitCh notification -> startStopReplication
Configuration-change case completes -> leaderLoop getState() == Leader guard
If guard permits another iteration: commitCh case -> getCommitIndex -> setCommitIndex -> processLogs
If guard rejects another iteration: leaderLoop exit -> runLeader deferred error responses and leader-state clearing
counterevidence: raft.go:1203:1283 verifies that dispatchLogs responds with the storage error and calls setState(Follower) before returning; it skips the local match report, last-log metadata update, and ordinary replication-trigger notifications.
commitment.go:1:104 verifies mutex serialization, increasing per-voter reports, and advancement only beyond the existing commitment index and at or above startIndex. New voters receive zero reports.
raft.go:1203:1361 verifies that processLogs skips already-applied indexes.
raft.go:442:850 verifies a role guard before each leader-loop select and a distinct commitCh case for commitment consumption and application scheduling.
raft.go:442:850 verifies admission only when latest and committed configuration indexes agree and the Raft commit index has reached this leadership's startIndex.

raft.go:442:850 verifies that deferred leader cleanup stops tracked replication, issues ErrLeadershipLost responses to inflight operations, and clears the commitment object and notification channel. Subsequent leader setup creates a fresh object and channel; caller-observed future results remain unverified.

Newly acquired raft.go:851:1010 resolves the configuration-handler continuation gap: the selected case invokes appendConfigurationEntry synchronously and ends immediately afterward. No commitment consumption or application scheduling intervenes before the next role guard.
unknowns: The previous missing-dispatch gap is resolved: configuration replacement proceeds after dispatchLogs returns, including its storage-error return.

The previous recalculation gap is resolved: setConfiguration retains surviving voter reports and recalculates immediately. Reachability of reports sufficient for advancement in the selected failure history remains unverified.

The previous handler-continuation gap is resolved by raft.go:851:1010. Whether setState(Follower) synchronously changes the state read by getState remains unread and is the remaining immediate discriminator.
Admission guards and their caller are now verified, but the applicable configuration activation contract remains incompletely established.
StoreLogs partial-write and durability semantics remain unknown; an error does not establish that nothing was stored.
startStopReplication can initiate or stop replication after failed dispatch. Effects outside the selected local commitment-consumption path remain unresolved.
Future response retention semantics remain unread; cleanup response calls alone do not establish the caller-observed result.
Previously scheduled FSM work and later follower or restart processing have not been shown to depend on this transient commitment advancement and remain outside the immediate discriminator.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: The acquired continuation confirms that control returns directly to the role guard. Verifying the role setter and getter is now the smallest causal dependency needed to determine whether that guard explains the suspected local consumption path.

selection_rationale: Continue F4 consumption. The requested leader-loop continuation was acquired completely and resolves the handler ordering question. A concrete protection is visible, but its decisive state-update semantics cannot be inferred from method names. Request the role helpers before disposing the suspicion; no obligation or model is justified yet.
